Contract.title: Contract
Contract.description: Represents a contract between a user and a client.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Contract entity.

folioNumber.description: Sequential contract number for tracking and auditing.

userId.description: Reference to the User who created the contract. (Relationship: User 1:N Contract)

clientId.description: Reference to the Client who is party to the contract. (Relationship: Client 1:N Contract)

clauses.description: The clauses and terms of the contract.

createdAt.description: The date and time the contract was created.

meetingDateTime.description: The date and time for a meeting related to the contract.

User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

Client.title: Client
Client.description: Represents a client associated with a contract.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Client entity.

Payment.title: Payment
Payment.description: Represents a financial transaction, such as a down payment or cancellation payment.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Payment entity.

paymentDate.description: The date and time the payment was made.

cancellationFolio.description: Sequential folio number specifically for cancellation payments.

updateFolio.description: Sequential folio number for certificate update payments.

clientId.description: Reference to the client who made the payment.

userId.description: Reference to the user who recorded the payment.

type.description: The type of payment (e.g., down payment, cancellation, update).

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore data structure has been updated to separate payment types into distinct collections: `cancellation_payments` and `update_payments`. This simplifies security rules and improves query performance for reports. By not having a single large `payments` collection, rules no longer need complex conditions to check the payment `type`, which was causing permission errors. Each new collection has simple, direct security rules, making the system more robust and easier to debug.
